transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

I came in because I can’t get past this feeling that I failed my brother. I’m an electrician—I’ve done this for years—and if I couldn’t keep him safe, then I keep thinking I’m a danger to anyone who works with me or even lives under my roof.
Can you tell me what happened with your brother?
I... I’m not sure I can talk about what happened yet. I just know I keep coming back to the fact that I was supposed to keep him safe, and I didn’t.
I understand it is hard to discuss what happened, but could you tell me roughly how long ago this took place?
About four months. Since the garage fire, and since my nephew came to live with us.
Since the fire, do you find yourself having unwanted, distressing memories or pictures of it suddenly popping into your head?

Yeah. I’ll be wiring a panel, or hear my nephew shut the garage door, and all of a sudden I’m back there—smelling the smoke and seeing my brother. It’s like everything around me just drops away for a second.
Do you find yourself actively avoiding places, conversations, or activities that remind you of the fire?

Yeah. I avoid the garage unless I absolutely have to go in there. I stopped helping with the electrical work at church, too. And if somebody starts talking about car projects or the fire, I usually just shut it down right away.
Since the fire, have you felt constantly on guard or unusually watchful of your surroundings?
I’m not really sure what you mean by constantly on guard. I haven’t paid much attention to that specifically.
Have you noticed yourself being unusually jumpy or easily startled by sudden sounds or movements?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether I’m more jumpy than usual.
Since the fire, have you been having trouble falling or staying asleep?

Yeah. Most nights I’m lying there listening for crackling, or a car door in the driveway. Then when I do get to sleep, I wake up soaked from dreams about the garage, and I can’t get back to sleep before work.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets diagnostic criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder following exposure to a traumatic event (a fatal/severe garage fire involving his brother 4 months ago). Symptoms include intrusive re-experiencing (flashbacks, distressing nightmares), avoidance of trauma-related reminders (avoiding the garage, avoiding conversations about the fire, stopping electrical work), persistent negative cognitions and self-blame, and marked sleep disturbances lasting for greater than one month.

confirmed_symptoms: Recurrent intrusive memories/flashbacks of smelling smoke and seeing brother
Distressing dreams related to the garage fire
Avoidance of external reminders including the garage
Avoidance of conversations about the fire and car projects
Avoidance of electrical activities (e.g., church electrical work)
Persistent distorted blame of self and excessive guilt regarding failing his brother and being a danger to others
Sleep disturbance including insomnia and waking up soaked from nightmares
